title: perf(canary): automated detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Ava Martinez

description: Motivation: reduce risk of deploying models or runtime changes that cause silent latency/throughput regressions. This PR introduces an automated performance canary detector and integration with rollout guards so canary regressions can automatically pause or rollback traffic shifts. Scope: - canary detector service that consumes existing latency/throughput metrics, buckets by model, instance type and sequence-length cohort, and performs statistical detection (Welch's t-test + bootstrap for p-value/CI) - hysteresis and sensitivity tuning so transient spikes don't trigger rollouts - integration with rollout controller to pause A/B/canary traffic when a regression is detected, with configurable thresholds per-release-channel - new perf-check CI job that runs a lightweight canary harness on CI for large PRs and nightly runs for baseline monitoring - dashboards and alerts: per-canary timelines, regression annotations, and runbook links Backwards compatibility: default sensitivity and rollout guard are conservative and off for older release channels; all configs are feature-flagged behind perf_canary_v2. Changes are confined to the perf-canary subsystem and rollout controller with minimal touchpoints to serving runtime.
